subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: Chapter 3. Insurance and Indemnification H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance 1. [3:645] Nature of Coverage: Directors and officers liability (D&O) insurance generally covers loss on account of claims against directors and officers based upon defined “wrongful acts” committed in their corporate capacity, which may include intentional misconduct (unlike CGL policies, which are based on an accidental “occurrence”; see ¶ 3:293). 2. [3:646] Typical Insuring Clause: “The Company shall pay on behalf of the Insured Persons [officers and directors] all Loss, for which such Insured Person is not indemnified by the Insured Organization [corporation], and which such Insured Person becomes legally obligated to pay on account of any claim[s] made against him, individually or otherwise … for a Wrongful Act … [c]ommitted … or attempted by such Insured Person[s] before or during the Policy Period; and … [r]eported to the Company … during the Policy Period …” [See Olson v. Federal Ins. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 252, 258, 268 CR 90, 92 (emphasis added; original emphasis omitted)] 3.
